T: Sydney, 1959. Continental food comes to the party.
D: A bookish teenager takes a summer job at a Sydney department store and is taken under the wing of its European staff.
P: Serve the mains when Magda welcomes everyone to her New Year's Eve party.
S: Salami, Hungarian sausage, pickled cucumbers, rye bread and soft cheese, the European spread that wowed 1959 Sydney.
lunch break upstairs at Goodes department store

Soft white bread with egg, mayo and cress, crusts off, cut into neat fingers for the ladies' tea. Boil 6 eggs for 10 minutes, cool, peel and mash with 4 tbsp mayonnaise, salt and pepper. Spread over 4 slices white bread, scatter with cress and top with 4 more slices. Trim the crusts and cut into fingers.
Magda introducing Lisa to continental food

Soft cheese whipped with butter, sweet paprika, capers, gherkin, onion and caraway into a bright orange spread, piled on dark rye with radish and chives. Beat 250g cream cheese (or quark) with 80g soft butter until smooth. Mix in 2 tsp sweet paprika, half a tsp caraway seeds, 1 tbsp chopped capers, 2 finely chopped gherkins, half a very finely diced small onion and 1 tsp Dijon. Season and chill 30 minutes. Spread thickly on 12 slices of dark rye, top with thinly sliced radish and chives and dust with a little more paprika.
M: the Hungarian cooking Fay falls for
Chicken thighs braised with onion, sweet paprika and capsicum, finished with sour cream, over buttered noodles.
Rudi, the Hungarian who wins Fay over

Red capsicums stuffed with beef and pork, rice, onion and smoked paprika, baked in a rich tomato sauce until soft, with sour cream and dill. Heat the oven to 180C. Cut the tops off 4 large red capsicums and seed them. Mix 300g beef mince, 200g pork mince, 150g cooked rice, 1 grated onion, 2 garlic cloves, 2 tsp sweet paprika, 1 tsp smoked paprika, 1 egg and salt. Pack into the capsicums and replace the lids. Stand in a dish with 700g passata mixed with 250ml stock and 1 tsp sugar. Cover and bake 1 hour, uncover for 15 minutes. Serve with sour cream and dill.
W: Lemon and poppy seed butter cake baked in a loaf tin and glazed with lemon icing. Beat 180g butter with 180g sugar, add 3 eggs and the zest of 2 lemons, then fold in 220g self-raising flour, 2 tbsp poppy seeds and 80ml milk. Bake in a loaf tin at 170C for 50 minutes. Ice with 150g icing sugar mixed with lemon juice.
K: Magda's New Year's Eve champagne punch

Cold sparkling wine poured over brandy, peach liqueur, orange and fresh peaches in a big punch bowl, a continental party trick for 1959 Sydney. In a large punch bowl, mix 60ml brandy, 60ml peach liqueur, 250ml fresh orange juice and 2 sliced ripe peaches. Chill 1 hour. Just before serving add a big block of ice and pour in a chilled 750ml bottle of sparkling wine and 250ml soda water. Stir once gently. Ladle into coupes with a slice of peach in each. For non-drinkers, use peach nectar and sparkling apple juice.

s.how: Slice 150g salami and 150g kabana and lay them out on a big board. Add 6 dill pickles cut into spears, 200g cream cheese in a bowl and a sliced dark rye loaf, the way Magda would set out a New Year's Eve spread.

m.how: Brown 1kg chicken thighs, then soften 2 onions and 1 red capsicum in the pan. Stir in 2 tbsp sweet paprika, add 375ml chicken stock and the chicken, and simmer 30 minutes. Stir 200g sour cream through off the heat and serve over 400g buttered egg noodles.
